disclaimer: Domain knowledge, not legal advice. Confirm applicability per jurisdiction with a qualified reviewer. No jurisdiction-specific rule (e.g. for Iran or any single country) is asserted here — only globally-published FATF/EU sources are cited, and every item is marked for human review.

items.name: KYC / Customer Due Diligence Thresholds
items.version: FATF baseline; exact monetary thresholds are set per jurisdiction
items.jurisdiction: varies by jurisdiction — FATF Recommendations set the baseline that national law implements
items.scope: Identity capture required above a transaction-amount threshold; enhanced due diligence above a second, higher threshold. No specific country's threshold amount is asserted here.
items.notes: This item deliberately does not name a threshold figure for any specific country (including Iran); a project must source its own jurisdiction's regulator for the exact amount.

items.name: AML — Suspicious / Large Transaction Reporting
items.jurisdiction: global (FATF member and cooperating jurisdictions); currency exchange offices are commonly named obliged entities
items.scope: Filing a suspicious transaction report (STR) or large-cash-transaction report with the relevant financial intelligence unit.
items.notes: Implemented differently per jurisdiction; verify the local financial intelligence unit's exact filing rules before building this feature into a product.

items.name: EU AML — Currency Exchange Offices as Obliged Entities
items.scope: Currency exchange offices ('bureaux de change') are named obliged entities subject to registration, CDD, and reporting duties.
items.notes: Applicability is staged under the 2024 EU AML package; verify current phase. Cited only for jurisdictions actually operating in the EU/EEA.

items.name: MSB Registration and Program Requirements (US)
items.version: 31 CFR Chapter X (FinCEN); registration via FinCEN Form 107
items.scope: A business that exchanges currency above the de minimis threshold is a money services business: it must register with FinCEN, renew that registration, maintain a written AML program with a designated compliance officer and independent review, keep records, and file the required reports. Whether a given operation is in scope, and the current de minimis figure, must be confirmed against FinCEN's own guidance.
items.notes: Applies only to US-facing operations. Nothing in this kit registers a business or constitutes an AML program; building the features below is not evidence of compliance.

provenance.notes: Sourced from FinCEN's own MSB resource page. Thresholds and scope tests were not transcribed here on purpose — they change and are the reviewer's job.

items.name: MSB Registration and Supervision (UK)
items.version: Money Laundering Regulations 2017 as amended; HMRC guidance AMLG2400 (MSB sector)
items.jurisdiction: United Kingdom (HMRC as supervisor; FCA for payment/e-money permissions)
items.scope: Currency exchange offices are supervised money service businesses: registration with HMRC, a risk assessment, customer due diligence, record keeping, and reporting. HMRC's MSB sector guidance sets out what supervisors expect to see.
items.notes: Applies only to UK-facing operations. Registration, fitness-and-propriety tests, and any FCA permission are outside anything software can satisfy.

provenance.notes: HMRC guidance is published under the Open Government Licence. Specific obligations were not transcribed verbatim; the URL is the authority.

items.name: PCI DSS — Cardholder Data
items.scope: Applies only where the product accepts, processes, transmits, or stores payment-card data — an online order-ahead flow taking a card, or a counter terminal integrated into the product. A cash-only bureau is out of scope. The cheapest posture is to never let card data touch the application (hosted fields or a terminal that tokenises), which changes which SAQ applies.
items.notes: Scope and the applicable Self-Assessment Questionnaire depend on how cards are taken; a QSA or the acquiring bank decides, not this catalog. Implementing tokenisation is not the same as being validated.

provenance.notes: Version 4.0.1 is the current published revision at the PCI SSC document library.
